extracted.intended_audience: readers of Charles Lamb; literary correspondents; students of 19th-century letters
extracted.subtask_description: Producing or reading humorous, informal early-19th-century literary letters and short essays (Charles Lamb / Elia style), with attention to tone, anecdote, and modest critical remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid repetition of consolatory religious topics
rubrics_metrics.description: If there be a cavil, it is that the topics of religious consolation, however beautiful, are repeated till a sort of triteness attends them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repetition of the same consolatory themes in multiple poems/addresses produces a sense of triteness; diversify or condense treatment of religious consolation to avoid cheapening the sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer concision in consolatory pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: One or two consolatory poems on deaths would have had a more condensed effect than many.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When treating bereavement or consolation, fewer, more concentrated pieces are often more effective than many scattered treatments that dilute impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive exotic/local colour
rubrics_metrics.description: You mostly cannot stir out (in such things) for humming-birds and fireflies. A tree is a Magnolia, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not overload verse or descriptive writing with exotic/local details merely for effect; overly frequent or forced local colour can spoil a poem's authenticity and distract the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not force allegory at the expense of character integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Why do you seem to sanction Landor's unfeeling allegorizing away of honest Quixote? He may as well say Strap is meant to symbolize the Scottish nation...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid interpreting or rewriting characters solely as symbols; heavy-handed allegorizing can betray the original character and reduce narrative richness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be clear and plausible with concrete details (avoid puzzling inconsistencies)
rubrics_metrics.description: We cannot make out how Edith should be no more than ten years old... By 'r Lady, we had taken her to be some sixteen or upwards. We suppose you have only chosen the round number for the metre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If choosing specific details (e.g., ages) for metrical or formal reasons, give some hint or context; unexplained inconsistencies puzzle readers and detract from credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use remote or improbable parallels judiciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is choicer in that sort of writing than to bring in some remote, impossible parallel,--as between a great empress and the inobtrusive, quiet soul who digged her noiseless way...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-chosen remote parallels can be a tasteful and effective device in praise or characterization, but they should be apt and not strained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of thought should determine order of writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The order of our thoughts should be the order of our writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a natural, logical sequence in composition—let the writer's train of thought guide the structure to preserve clarity and sincerity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inadvertent personal applications or unnamed attacks
rubrics_metrics.description: My tirade against visitors was not meant particularly at you or Anne Knight... So in another thing I talked of somebody's insipid wife without a correspondent object in my head; and a good lady... has looked shyly on me ever since.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing satire or criticism, take care not to make remarks that unintentionally target acquaintances; accidental personal application leads to ludicrous blunders and hurt feelings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value plainness and singleness of manner
rubrics_metrics.description: In him seem to have died the old plainness of manners and singleness of heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple, unpretentious expression and a straightforward tone (plainness of manner) are virtues in writing and character portrayal; they create trust and warmth with readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve original tone when reprinting classics; avoid garish modernization
rubrics_metrics.description: Stop thy friend's sacrilegious hand. Nothing can be done for B. but to reprint the old cuts in as homely but good a style as possible... How unlike his own! ... show and emptiness 'yclept "Annuals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When editing or republishing classic works, retain the original illustrative style and modesty rather than over-fashionable or incongruous embellishments that undermine the author's spirit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose worthy source material for adaptation
rubrics_metrics.description: I would strongly recommend you to take for one story Massinger's 'Old Law.' It is exquisite. I can think of no other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select high-quality, well-suited source texts when adapting or basing new works on older material; a judicious choice of source will improve the resulting piece.
